codeReview.summary: Verified the committed feature (bc4326f7) plus the current on-disk state. Positives: packages/tenant-db/drizzle/0016_reservations_foundation.sql creates exactly the 41 rsv_* tables the contract enumerates (contract line 64 says '30' but lists 41), all 41 are exported as Drizzle tables (packages/tenant-db/src/schema.ts 'export const rsv*' count = 41; packages/tenant-db/src/index.ts re-exports schema.ts), the contract's CHECK constraints are present (chk_rsv_tables_covers/chk_rsv_table_combos_covers for 1<=min_covers<=max_covers<=99, chk_rsv_tables_reset_buffer 0..120, chk_rsv_services_seating_order and _max_span, end_at>start_at on blocks/holds/reservations/occupancies, party_size 1..99 on holds/reservations/notify_requests/waitlist_entries, single-owner checks on rsv_service_availability, rsv_blocks and rsv_table_occupancies), rsv_reservations.hold_id is UNIQUE (line 531), and apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts is regenerated and byte-in-sync with 0016 (m0000..m0016 present; the sync assertion passes). Control plane: packages/database/drizzle/0025_reservations_foundation.sql seeds the same 8 permissions as RESERVATIONS_PERMISSIONS with org_role_admin grants only, mirrors them in setup-roles.ts, @repo/auth ORG_PERMISSIONS and @repo/security PERMISSIONS, and inserts the 6 system-level reservations.* ConfigFlag rows with value='false' via per-key INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS. Read-only checks confirm applied state: data.db and local D1 each have the 8 Permission rows, 8 _OrganizationPermissionToRole rows for org_role_admin (0 for org_role_member), 1 system false row per flag key; both tenant DBs (packages/database/db/tenant_t58bgatqh3rv0s3movrecyj1.db and packages/database/db/ksa/tenant_ru0dm42cud9scs4g2duep21c.db) report 41 rsv_* tables and 9 rsv_* triggers; apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts exists on disk. I re-ran packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts (CI=true, 6/6 passed). Blocking problems are all in the hand-appended trigger block: the two occupancy-overlap triggers are stricter than the contract/architecture (they abort a normal occupancy that overlaps an existing staff overbook row, a configuration the domain engine explicitly permits) and they raise 'table_overlap' instead of the contract's 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap'. One blocking test-hygiene problem: the new DO-bundle sync test reads a gitignored artifact from another workspace that no test-task dependency generates.

issues.description: The occupancy overlap triggers are stricter than the approved contract. VAL-FND-011 (validation-contract.md line 70) and architecture section 4.8 (architecture.md:902-921) both require the abort predicate to match another row with `active = 1 AND overbook = 0`; the shipped triggers filter only `o.active = 1` and omit `o.overbook = 0` in the insert trigger (line 810) and update trigger (line 824; this one also drops the architecture's WHEN narrowing). Consequence: an active, non-overbook occupancy that overlaps an existing active overbook row is rejected, although the contract says 'explicit staff overbook rows (overbook = 1) succeed without triggering an abort'. Reproduced with the file's own trigger SQL in a throwaway SQLite DB: after inserting an overbook row [1000,2000) on table t1, `INSERT INTO rsv_table_occupancies VALUES ('occ_norm','t1','reservation','r2',NULL,NULL,1500,2500,1,0)` fails with `Error: stepping, table_overlap (19)`; per the contract it must succeed. This contradicts the module's own capacity model, which deliberately ignores overbook rows when deciding whether a table is free: packages/reservations/src/engine/occupancy.ts:94,117,166 (`if (entry.overbook) continue`) and the I2 oracle pair check packages/reservations/src/testing/oracle.ts:114 (`if (a.overbook || b.overbook) continue`). So a staff-channel assignment (or a bounded repair/reflow) that the engine plans and re-validates as a normal placement on a table carrying an active overbook row will fail at the DB write - the safety net rejects a legal mutation instead of catching an illegal one. The added test only covers inserting a NEW overbook = 1 row (packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts:1219-1232), so the diverging case is untested.

Abort-message mismatch against the contract. VAL-FND-011 requires the trigger to abort with 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap' (validation-contract.md line 70) and architecture section 4.8 shows `RAISE(ABORT, 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap')` (architecture.md:906,919); the shipped triggers raise 'table_overlap' (lines 806 and 819) and the test asserts that string (packages/tenant-db/src/reservations-schema.test.ts:1177, 1210, 1251). No code in the repo consumes the contract string or the shipped string (the only trigger-message consumer, apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:575, matches 'overlap_conflict'), so this is a conformance/diagnostics mismatch rather than a runtime break today. Note that later mission artifacts authored after this feature use 'table_overlap' too (docs/decisions/048-reservations-data-residency.md:149, docs/reservations-plan.md:23), so the validator may instead decide to amend architecture section 4.8 / the contract; per the review rules the contract governs, in which case the two RAISE strings plus the three test expectations must change together.

The new DO-bundle sync test couples the @repo/tenant-db suite to a gitignored artifact owned by another workspace and does an unguarded `readFileSync` of it (line 138-144), so the suite cannot run on a clean checkout. apps/tenant-api/workers/migrations.generated.ts is ignored by apps/tenant-api/.gitignore:1 and is generated only by tenant-api's build/typecheck/deploy (`generate:do-migrations`, apps/tenant-api/package.json). Turbo's test task only depends on `^build` (turbo.json .tasks.test), and tenant-api is not a dependency of @repo/tenant-db, so nothing generates the file for this suite; in CI the parallel vitest job (.github/workflows/deploy.yml:173-215) runs `npm run test` with no tenant-api build step, and no tenant-api test imports workers/tenant-org.ts (only org-router.ts/bindings.ts), so the file will not exist and `npm test -w @repo/tenant-db` fails with ENOENT. It passes here only because the worker had already generated the file in this sandbox. Fix by generating the bundle inside the test setup (preferred, keeps the sync assertion) or by asserting on a path whose task dependency generates it.

rsv_holds_single_conversion is narrower than the contract: it uses `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted' AND NEW.status = 'converted'`, so it aborts only a re-conversion, while VAL-FND-012 says it 'aborts any UPDATE on a rsv_holds row whose OLD.status = converted' and architecture section 4.8 specifies `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted'`. An UPDATE that moves a converted hold's status away from 'converted' (or edits other columns while flipping the status) is currently accepted. No milestone code path updates converted holds, and the at-most-once guarantee is still enforced for the normal flow by the UNIQUE index on rsv_reservations.hold_id (line 531), so this is latent; tightening the WHEN clause to `WHEN OLD.status = 'converted'` would match the contract exactly.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Trigger-abort message strings and error mapping are inconsistent across the mission's artifacts, and no canonical convention is recorded. architecture.md section 4.8 uses 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap' (architecture.md:906,919) and the validation contract repeats it, while docs/decisions/048-reservations-data-residency.md:149-156 (written later) uses 'table_overlap'/'hold_overlap' and refers to triggers that do not exist in the shipped 0016 (named trg_rsv_*, a holds-overlap trigger, and a `payload -> NULL` redaction shape instead of the shipped `data = '{"redacted":true}'`), docs/reservations-plan.md:23-25 uses 'table_overlap'/'hold_overlap', and apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:575 maps 'overlap_conflict'. Suggest the mission library or AGENTS.md record the canonical trigger names/messages and the trigger-message-to-HTTP mapping so workers stop diverging. Note this ADR/impl divergence also affects the docs feature (VAL-FND-024) and should be reconciled there.

Worth adding to the library so later workers run the generator (or build tenant-api) before tests that read the bundle.

The handoff's skillFeedback flags a real local-tooling quirk worth recording next to commands.migrate_control_plane (library/environment.md:76): `wrangler d1 migrations apply DB --local` fails with `SQLITE_ERROR: too many terms in compound SELECT` when a control-plane migration uses a multi-branch UNION ALL inside `INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS`; the worker wrote one INSERT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS statement per flag instead, which applies cleanly to both data.db and local D1. Adding this to library/environment.md would save the next worker the same debugging.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Two contract wordings can produce false validator failures and should be treated as known contract text issues: VAL-FND-010 (validation-contract.md:64) says 'all 30 rsv_* tables' but enumerates 41 names, and the implementation has exactly those 41; VAL-FND-013's evidence query (validation-contract.md:85) filters `WHERE A LIKE 'org_perm_%'`, but in _OrganizationPermissionToRole A is the role id and B the permission id (packages/database/src/schema.ts:1122-1140), so the contract's query returns 0 rows even though the seeded grants are correct. Read-only check: `SELECT A,B FROM _OrganizationPermissionToRole WHERE B LIKE '%reservation%'` returns exactly 8 rows, all A='org_role_admin'; `SELECT COUNT(*) ... WHERE A='org_role_member' AND B LIKE '%reservation%'` returns 0.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Out-of-scope but worth routing to the tenant-api write-gate feature review: mapSqliteConstraintError (apps/tenant-api/src/lib/reservations-write.ts:571-581) matches 'overlap_conflict', 'hold_already_converted' and 'uniq_rsv_reservations_hold_id', none of which matches the actual trigger text for overlap ('table_overlap' / the contract's 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap') or SQLite's UNIQUE failure text for the hold index ('UNIQUE constraint failed: rsv_reservations.hold_id'). Architecture section 8 promises 'a trigger abort maps to 409 conflict', so today a trigger abort surfaces as an unmapped error. The reviewed feature's trigger strings are the interface this mapping must target, so whichever string the validator settles on should also be wired into that mapping.

summary: Reviewed fnd-migrations-tenant-and-control-plane (commit bc4326f7, worker 5a4e43b1, backend-worker skill; procedure matched the skill, no deviations). The structural parts of the contract pass: 41/41 rsv_* tables with Drizzle exports, the required CHECK constraints and single-owner checks, hold_id UNIQUE, 9 triggers, an in-sync regenerated DO bundle, the 8 seeded permissions with org_role_admin-only grants mirrored in setup-roles.ts/@repo/auth/@repo/security plus a zero-drift test, and 6 system-level false ConfigFlag rows inserted idempotently; applied state verified read-only in data.db, local D1 and both tenant SQLite DBs, and the targeted schema test passes 6/6. Verdict: fail. Blocking: (1) the two occupancy-overlap triggers omit the contract's required `o.overbook = 0` predicate (lines 810/824), so a normal occupancy overlapping an existing staff overbook row aborts even though VAL-FND-011 says it must succeed and the domain engine deliberately treats overbook rows as non-blocking (reproduced empirically); (2) the triggers raise 'table_overlap' instead of the contract/architecture string 'rsv_table_occupancies overlap'; (3) the new DO-bundle sync test (reservations-schema.test.ts:131) reads a gitignored tenant-api build artifact with no generator in the test dependency graph, so @repo/tenant-db's suite cannot run on a clean checkout or in CI's vitest job. Non-blocking: rsv_holds_single_conversion's WHEN clause is narrower than VAL-FND-012 ('converted'->'converted' only), latent today because hold_id UNIQUE still protects the single-conversion guarantee.
